Sampler Settings

Core Settings
Temperature
Controls creativity. Higher = more random.
Good for: Storytelling, brainstorming, character dialogue.
Example: Higher temp → "The dragon laughs and offers tea."
Warning: None.
Enabled
Top‑P Conflicts with Min‑P, Typical‑P, Top‑A
Filters tokens by cumulative probability.
Good for: Focused output.
Example: 0.9 → 90% probability mass.
Warning: Conflicts with Min‑P, Typical‑P, Top‑A.
Top‑K
Only allows the top K most likely tokens.
Good for: More deterministic output.
Example: K=40 → stable but flexible.
Warning: None.
Min‑P Conflicts with Top‑P, Typical‑P
Filters tokens below minimum probability.
Good for: Quality filtering.
Example: 0.05 → removes low-prob tokens.
Warning: Conflicts with Top‑P and Typical‑P.
Repeat Penalty
Penalizes repeated tokens.
Good for: Preventing loops.
Example: Stops "Hello hello hello…"
Warning: Too high makes writing weird.
Repeat Last‑N
How far back repetition is checked.
Good for: Long‑form writing.
Example: 64 → good for chat.
Warning: Very high values slow generation.
Intermediate Controls
Enabled
Presence Penalty Conflicts with Frequency Penalty
Penalizes new topics (reduces topic drift).
Good for: Staying on topic.
Example: 0.3 → stay focused.
Warning: Conflicts with Frequency Penalty.
Enabled
Frequency Penalty Conflicts with Presence Penalty
Penalizes tokens based on frequency.
Good for: Avoiding repeated words.
Example: Stops "very very very."
Warning: Conflicts with Presence Penalty.
Enabled
Typical‑P Conflicts with Top‑P
Filters tokens by typical probability.
Good for: Natural‑sounding text.
Example: 1.0 = no filtering.
Warning: Conflicts with Top‑P.
Advanced Controls
Enabled
Mirostat Mode Overrides Temperature, Top‑P, Typical‑P
Auto‑tunes sampling parameters.
Good for: Consistent perplexity.
Example: Mode 2 for stable long‑form.
Warning: Overrides Temperature, Top‑P, Typical‑P.
Mirostat Tau
Target perplexity for Mirostat.
Good for: Controlling surprise.
Example: 5.0 = balanced.
Warning: Lower = more predictable.
Mirostat Eta
Learning rate for Mirostat.
Good for: Adaptation speed.
Example: 0.1 = standard.
Warning: Higher = faster adaptation.
Enabled
Dynamic Temperature Range Can conflict with Mirostat
Adjusts temperature based on token probability.
Good for: Adaptive creativity.
Example: More varied on low‑prob tokens.
Warning: Can conflict with Mirostat.
Dynamic Temperature Exponent
Exponent for dynamic temperature calculation.
Good for: Fine-tuning adaptation.
Example: 1.0 = linear.
Warning: Higher = more aggressive.
DRY Multiplier
Penalty for repetition in output.
Good for: Preventing repetition.
Example: 0.5 = moderate penalty.
Warning: Too high breaks flow.
DRY Allowed Length
Minimum length before DRY applies.
Good for: Short phrases.
Example: 2 = words.
Warning: None.
DRY Base
Base penalty for DRY.
Good for: Fine-tuning DRY.
Example: 1.0 = standard.
Warning: None.
Seed
Controls randomness.
Good for: Reproducible outputs.
Example: Same seed = same story.
Warning: -1 = random.

Model Settings

Core Model Settings
Reasoning (thinking models)
Thinking models reason before answering. On shows the thought in a collapsible block; Hidden uses it without showing it; Off answers directly. Takes effect the next time a model loads.
Model Family
Auto-detected from GGUF metadata
Good for: Ensuring correct prompt format and tokenizer.
Example: LLaMA → LLaMA template, Mistral → Mistral template.
Warning: None.
Model Variant
Auto-detected from GGUF metadata
Good for: Auto-configuring safe performance defaults.
Example: 7B → 8K context, 4 threads. 70B → 32K context, 16 threads.
Warning: None.
Thread Count Too high = system lag
CPU parallelism
Good for: Maximizing CPU utilization without lag.
Example: 12-core CPU → 11 threads.
Warning: Too high = system lag.
Batch Size Too high = out-of-memory crash
Tokens processed per step
Good for: Faster token generation.
Example: 512 = balanced. 2048 = fast but RAM-heavy.
Warning: Too high = out-of-memory crash.
GPU Offload Layers Exceeds VRAM = crash
Moves layers to GPU for speed
Good for: Speeding up generation with a GPU.
Example: 33 layers on a 33-layer model = fully GPU.
Warning: Exceeds VRAM = crash.
Performance Settings
KV Cache Size Too high = RAM exhaustion
Tokens stored before eviction
Good for: Long conversations without eviction.
Example: 4096 = 4K tokens cached.
Warning: Too high = RAM exhaustion.
KV Cache Type
How KV cache is stored/managed
Good for: Optimizing memory vs speed tradeoff.
Example: Flash-Attention = fastest. Paged = most flexible.
Warning: None.
Rope Scaling Mode Wrong mode = degraded coherence
Extends usable context window
Good for: Extending context beyond training length.
Example: LLaMA 3 → Dynamic. LFM → Linear.
Warning: Wrong mode = degraded coherence.
Rope Factor Too high = positional confusion
How aggressively to scale positional embeddings
Good for: Fine-tuning context extension aggressiveness.
Example: 1.0 = no scaling. 2.0 = 2x context.
Warning: Too high = positional confusion.
Tensor Split Mismatched GPUs = inefficiency
Multi-GPU partitioning
Good for: Multi-GPU load balancing.
Example: 50 = half on GPU 0, half on GPU 1.
Warning: Mismatched GPUs = inefficiency.
Memory & Context Settings
Max Context Window Exceeds model training = incoherence
Auto-detected from GGUF metadata
Good for: Long-form writing and memory.
Example: 4096 = ~3000 words of context.
Warning: Exceeds model training = incoherence.
Context Rollover Mode
How context is trimmed
Good for: Keeping important context during rollover.
Example: Memory-Guided preserves lore and character facts.
Warning: None.
Memory Integration
Enables memory system to guide post-rollover
Good for: Maintaining story continuity.
Example: On = memories survive context rollover.
Warning: None.
Enabled
System Prompt Cache
Keeps system prompt pinned in KV cache
Good for: Faster repeated system prompts.
Example: On = system prompt stays cached after rollover.
Warning: None.
Enabled
Prompt & Template Settings
Prompt Template Wrong template = garbled output
Auto-detected from GGUF metadata
Good for: Correct chat formatting.
Example: ChatML → <|im_start|>user / <|im_start|>assistant.
Warning: Wrong template = garbled output.
Custom Jinja Template Overrides Prompt Template selection
Full manual override
Good for: Models with unusual chat templates.
Example: {{ bos_token }} {% for message in messages %}{{ message.role }}...
Warning: Overrides Prompt Template selection.
System Prompt Override
Replaces the model's default system prompt
Good for: Forcing a specific persona or behavior.
Example: "You are a helpful coding assistant."
Warning: None.
User Prompt Prefix
Adds a prefix to every user message
Good for: Marking user input in instruct models.
Example: "### Instruction:\n"
Warning: None.
Assistant Prompt Prefix
Adds a prefix to every assistant message
Good for: Marking assistant output in instruct models.
Example: "### Response:\n"
Warning: None.
Stop Sequences Too many = premature halting
Controls where generation halts
Good for: Stopping generation at specific tokens.
Example: ", <|endoftext|>, Human:"
Warning: Too many = premature halting.
Tokenizer Override Wrong tokenizer = broken output
For models with mismatched tokenizers
Good for: Fixing tokenization mismatches.
Example: SentencePiece for LLaMA, TikToken for GPT.
Warning: Wrong tokenizer = broken output.

Directory locator

Looking for model files… Scanning reads metadata only

New model folder detected

First scan

Howl Chat found a model directory that hasn't been scanned before.

What happens when you scan?

  • Finds model files in this folder.
  • Identifies their architectures and capabilities.
  • Determines which models are usable for chat, voice, image generation, and other supported tasks.
  • Organizes them into the appropriate model pickers.
New directory —

Scanning inspects model files. It does not load models into memory, start inference, or reserve VRAM.

You can change this preference later in Settings.
